downloadedSourceCountNote: Zero is correct. All four current binaries plus one superseded revision were retrieved into temporary storage outside the repository and outside every worktree for provenance and measurement, and all were discarded. Nothing entered version control, no materialization destination was written and no receipt was created — this job owns no authority asset path and no receipt path. The provenance and hashes the assignment requires are recorded below as measurements, not as deposits.

method.description: Public official download and supersession reconstruction. The controlling source is the Florida Administrative Code at flrules.org, because FDLE's expunction applications are not published as free-standing agency forms but are incorporated by reference into Chapter 11C-7 rules, each with its own Ref-NNNNN identifier and adoption date. Each rule's incorporation history was walked to reconstruct the full supersession chain, then the current binary for each of the four assigned identities was retrieved, hashed and measured, and its printed revision block and rule citation were read from the form face.
method.controllingSource: https://www.flrules.org — the official Florida Administrative Code
method.controllingSourceRationale: FDLE's own web pages never print a form number. The numbers 40-021, 40-025, 40-026 and 40-028 exist only in the FAC incorporation records, so the FAC is the only place where these identities are citable at all.
method.tooling: curl for retrieval and HTTP status; sha256 and byte counts on the retrieved bytes; poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for structure and face text; pdf-lib for AcroForm, annotation and page-geometry reads
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires using only the assigned public official sources, recording provenance and hashes, and stopping where identity, revision or issuer authority is uncertain. All four identities resolved with certainty on all three axes, so none was stopped. Two defects were found in the official material itself and are recorded as findings rather than treated as uncertainty.
method.scopeBoundary: This job covers the four FDLE agency-stage applications only. It does not touch the Rule 3.989 court-stage identities, which are a separate assigned job currently being integrated, and it does not touch the Rule 3.989 continuation identity resolved earlier.

incorporatingRules.keyFinding: The four forms are not incorporated by one rule. Each has its own rule, and one form is incorporated twice under two different rules. All five rules share an 8/30/2023 effective date, which is a re-adoption date and not a form revision date.

noLaterRulemaking.how: Every one of the five rules' notice tables on flrules.org ends at the 8/30/2023 final adoption. No pending or proposed amendment exists as of 2026-08-08.
noLaterRulemaking.caveat: Absence of a proposed amendment today is not a guarantee against one tomorrow. Recorded as of the retrieval date.

ruleDateVersusFormDate.trap: Rule 11C-7.006 is effective 8/30/2023 and recites 'form number FDLE 40-021, rev. June 2021', while the Ref-14423 landing page displays an adoption date of 08/30/2023.
ruleDateVersusFormDate.resolution: Both are correct in their own frame. The 2023 rulemaking re-adopted forms whose printed revision dates did not change. The form's identity date is its printed revision; the rule's adoption date is 8/30/2023. Record both and never substitute one for the other.
ruleDateVersusFormDate.consequence: A revision field populated from the rule's effective date would record every one of these forms as a 2023 revision, which is wrong for all four.

doTheFourCollapse.question: Are these four genuinely four distinct forms, or do some collapse into one another?
doTheFourCollapse.answer: Four distinct forms, four distinct form numbers, four distinct rules. None collapses.
doTheFourCollapse.basis: Answered from the FAC incorporation list rather than by inference. Each form is incorporated by its own rule at its own Ref id.
doTheFourCollapse.selfDefenseIsSeparate: FDLE 40-026 is its own form under its own rule 11C-7.012. It is not a section or a variant of 40-021. This has been true only since 5-5-2020; before that it was incorporated under 11C-7.006 alongside 40-021 and, in Ref-05634 and Ref-10784, filed as a single bundled reference document. Anything sourced from that era will appear to collapse them.
doTheFourCollapse.theTwoJuvenileFormsAreSeparate: 40-025 (diversion, s. 943.0582, rule 11C-7.009) and 40-028 (early juvenile, s. 943.0515, rule 11C-7.010) differ in form number, rule, Ref id, eligibility, prosecutor certification and fee treatment.

theRealCollapseRunsTheOtherWay.finding: FDLE 40-021 is a single dual-purpose form serving both sealing and expunction, and it is incorporated twice — Ref-14423 under 11C-7.006 and Ref-14424 under 11C-7.007.
theRealCollapseRunsTheOtherWay.verifiedByMeasurement: Both Ref ids were retrieved separately and both returned 232,916 bytes at sha256 7a3647f5…b8ee8. Byte-identical, same filename.
theRealCollapseRunsTheOtherWay.corroboratedOnTheFace: The form's own footer reads 'Ref. Rule 11C-7.006 and 11C-7.007' — the issuer prints the dual incorporation on the artifact.
theRealCollapseRunsTheOtherWay.consequence: The certificate-of-eligibility identity has two equally official current Ref ids. Pick one deliberately and record why. For an expunction route the correct citation is Ref-14423; for sealing it is Ref-14424. The bytes are the same either way, so this is a citation choice, not a source choice.
theRealCollapseRunsTheOtherWay.warning: Do not create two edition rows for one form. One document, one digest, two incorporations.

defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.finding: The currently incorporated FDLE 40-025 is a change-marked comparison copy, not a clean form. Its filename is literally 'FDLE 40-025 Juvenile Diversion Expunction Application Marked Up.pdf', and its footer prints both revision dates: 'Revised October 2019 July 2022', with the older date struck through and the newer inserted. The certification page carries underlined inserted statutory text.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.verifiedByMeasurement: The extracted text of the retrieved binary shows 'Revised October 2019 July 2022' in the footer of every footer-bearing page, which is the redline rendered flat.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.consequence: Any packet reproducing Ref-15824 faithfully will reproduce the strikethroughs and underlines to a participant. This is the officially incorporated version, so substituting a clean copy from elsewhere would be substituting a document the FAC does not incorporate.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.notResolvedHere: Whether to reproduce the redline, seek a clean copy from FDLE, or flag it to counsel is a legal-design and acquisition decision outside this assignment.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.doNotSilentlyClean: Do not regenerate or re-flatten the file to remove the markup. That would create bytes no official source publishes.

defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.finding: FDLE 40-021 page 1 prints 'EXPUNCTION (s. 943.585, F.S.)'. The correct citation is s. 943.0585. The typo is FDLE's and is present in both the October 2019 and the current June 2021 revisions.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.consequence: An official title recorded verbatim will contain the typo. Recording a corrected citation would produce a title string that does not match the artifact. Record the verbatim face string and note the correction separately.

defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.finding: The measured file is 6 pages, but the application pages print 'Page 1 of 2' and 'Page 2 of 2'. The fingerprint sheet and the instruction pages sit outside the form's own numbering. The superseded Ref-11937 is worse: it prints 'Page 3 of 2'.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.consequence: Any page-count validation keyed on the printed 'of N' will fail against the true page count. Use the measured count.

defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.finding: FDLE's own web pages do not print '40-021', '40-025', '40-026' or '40-028' anywhere. The form numbers exist only in the Florida Administrative Code.
defectsInTheOfficialMaterial.consequence: A worker sourcing from fdle.state.fl.us rather than flrules.org obtains an unnumbered, uncitable artifact. The FAC must remain the controlling source for identity.

commercialUseAndLicensing.flrulesOrg: The only copyright text anywhere on flrules.org is the footer line 'Copyright @ 2010 State of Florida Department of State'. There is no terms-of-use page, no licence and no reuse or commercial-use statement on the homepage or the about page.
commercialUseAndLicensing.fdleStateFlUs: No copyright notice, terms of use or reuse restriction on the Seal and Expunge pages. https://www.fdle.state.fl.us/Disclaimer returns HTTP 404.
commercialUseAndLicensing.theBinariesThemselves: None of the four carries a copyright, licence or reuse legend on any page.
commercialUseAndLicensing.conclusion: Silence, not permission. No affirmative grant of reuse or commercial-distribution rights exists on either site, and the bare 'Copyright @ 2010 State of Florida Department of State' line is a weak assertion of rights rather than a waiver.
commercialUseAndLicensing.doNotInfer: Public downloadability is not a licence. generationAllowed must not be set true on the strength of this record.
commercialUseAndLicensing.escalation: If commercial redistribution matters, this needs counsel or a written FDLE or Department of State response. That is a human-only task and it was not attempted.
commercialUseAndLicensing.queueRecordedPosition: The queue records no commercial-use question for these rows; this record supplies the finding it lacked.

correctionsToTheTaskPremise.verified: s. 943.0583 is 'Human trafficking victim expunction'. It mentions no FDLE form and no certificate of eligibility, and no Chapter 11C-7 rule implements it. The self-defense statute is s. 943.0578, implemented by rule 11C-7.012.
correctionsToTheTaskPremise.consequence: A record citing 943.0583 for self-defense would point the Florida self-defense track at the human-trafficking statute. Note that human trafficking is the same carve-out that produced Fla. R. Crim. P. 3.9895 on the court side, so the two are easy to cross.

correctionsToTheTaskPremise.recorded: The juvenile provisions are at s. 985.255.
correctionsToTheTaskPremise.verified: The juvenile authorities actually implemented are s. 943.0515(1) (early juvenile) and s. 943.0582 (diversion), the latter cross-referencing the diversion programme at s. 985.3065, formerly s. 985.125.
correctionsToTheTaskPremise.consequence: s. 985.255 is a detention statute and is not implemented by any of these rules.

feeFinding.statutoryBasisFor40021: s. 943.0585(2) provides for it: 'Remits a $75 processing fee to the department… unless the executive director waives such fee.'
feeFinding.contradiction: s. 943.0578 (self-defense) contains no fee provision, yet FDLE's self-defense page and the form's own checklist require the $75 fee. Treat the fee as rule- or practice-imposed for self-defense, not statutory.
feeFinding.exception: The checklist states the fee is not required for juvenile diversion expunction applications.
feeFinding.notDecidedHere: The fee's legal basis for the self-defense route is recorded as a contradiction, not resolved. It is a legal-design question.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. All four identities, issuers, roles, revisions, scopes and current binaries are established from the controlling official source, with hashes, and the full supersession chain is reconstructed for each. It is not fully cleared, because the successor edition retains none of them and because the commercial-use question is unresolved by silence rather than answered.
terminalDispositionDetail.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Retrievability is proven and the digests are pinned. What remains is an edition decision, not an acquisition.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Four Florida FDLE identities move from authority_unmanifested_source with unconfirmed revisions to fully identified, hashed and measured current binaries with complete supersession chains, official URLs and HTTP evidence. Edition 1.3 gains four ready-to-add rows with digests, byte counts, page counts and structural class supplied. Nine superseded Ref ids are named as live traps, and the fingerprint-sentence discriminator gives a one-line current-versus-stale test for the most-used form. Two errors in the recorded statutory basis are corrected, including one that would have pointed the self-defense track at the human-trafficking statute. The redline defect in the officially incorporated juvenile diversion form is surfaced before it can reach a participant packet. No component is rebound, no receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no renderer is assigned, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
